p: "And it was on the third day,
that there were thunders and lightnings,
and a heavy cloud upon the mountain,
וְקוֹל שׁוֹפָר חָזָק מְאוֹד (שְׁמוֹת יט, טז).
and the sound of the shofar, exceedingly strong" (Shemos 19:16).
This was said before Matan Torah;
and after Matan Torah it says:
"And all the people see the thunders,
and the sound of the shofar,
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פא, ב)
but once it was set in its proper arrangement
The meaning is that at the beginning,
the revelation of holiness to a person
is only like the flash of lightning
before the eye for a moment,
And in place of the "heavy cloud"
there is mentioned after Matan Torah
and smoke is a greater darkness than cloud,
וְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פא, א):
And it says in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 81a):
and that sound of the shofar
came forth from the innermost of them all."
at the beginning of the revelation,
meaning that they merited the flash
of the revelation of His light, Yisbarach.
כִּי לֹא יִרְאַנִי הָאָדָם וְגוֹ׳ (שְׁמוֹת לג, כ),
"For no man shall see Me, etc." (Shemos 33:20),
in order that they not be nullified out of existence
through the revelation of His light, Yisbarach,
there had to be a contraction —
the light could be grasped by the recipient
without his being nullified out of existence.
which is a darkness of tangible substance.
And thick mist is the contraction
וּמֹשֶׁה נִגַּשׁ אֶל הָעֲרָפֶל (שְׁמוֹת כ, יח);
"And Moshe drew near to the thick mist" (Shemos 20:18);
כִּי הֲגַם שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
for although Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom,
פֶּה אֶל פֶּה אֲדַבֶּר בּוֹ (בַּמִּדְבָּר יב, ח),
"Mouth to mouth I speak with him" (Bamidbar 12:8),
his soul and his body were exceedingly refined,
with a thin contraction like thick mist,
so that there would be grasped by him
he would not be nullified out of existence.
the contraction of the heavy cloud,
"and the sound of the shofar, exceedingly strong";
there could branch out in the soul
for the arousal of the sound of the shofar,
which brings trembling into a person's heart,
to rouse him from the sleep
"And it shall be on that day
that a great shofar shall be sounded,
that is, the special power of the sound of the shofar
serves to gather in the outcasts
it is stated in the words:
מִפְּנֵי אֲשֶׁר יָרַד עָלָיו ה׳ בָּאֵשׁ,
because Hashem descended upon it in fire,
and its smoke went up, etc." (Shemos 19:18).
That is, when they came to a greater revelation,
because on account of the great contraction
so that there not branch out from it
the sound of the shofar had to be
in order to rouse him all the more,
so that even darkness would not darken,
וְכִדְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב פא, א):
And as it says in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 81a):
"'And the sound of the shofar, exceedingly strong' —
'And it was, when you heard the voice
out of the midst of the darkness' (Devarim 5:20)."
Now after Matan Torah it says:
"And all the people see the thunders,
and the flames, and the sound of the shofar,
and the people saw and trembled" (Shemos 20:15).
Seemingly the two words "and the people saw"
while "saw" is in the past tense.
is truly in the present tense,
that all the souls of Yisrael
have the power at all times
And "the people saw and trembled, etc."
is a kind of giving of the reason
"And Moshe said, Do not fear, etc.,
so that His fear be upon your faces,
which brings one to fear of sin;
it is certain that his forefathers did not stand
to his forefathers' standing at Mount Sinai?
for the wording "all the people see"
there was absorbed into the souls of Yisrael
and it comes to give the reason for this —
meaning then, at the time of Matan Torah,
when his forefathers stood at Mount Sinai,
which is only for this reason:
so that this seeing be fixed
as in the Gemara's exposition cited above.
in the pasuk "And all the people see,"
which alludes to the power of revelation for all generations;
the sound of the shofar, and the smoking mountain.
And they correspond to the three middos
who is the fourth leg, as is known.
That is: the aspect of thunders
יוֹרֶה עַל מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
indicates the middah of Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
who began to stir himself in his soul
לִרְאוֹת מִי בָרָא אֵלֶּה (יְשַׁעְיָה מ, כו),
that this is the aspect of the beginning
and as the pasuk says about him:
מִי הֵעִיר מִמִּזְרָח וְגוֹ׳ (יְשַׁעְיָה מא, ב).
"Who aroused one from the east, etc." (Yeshayah 41:2).
And this comes from the power of the bas kol
in the name of the holy Baal Shem Tov,
there comes an awakening to teshuvah
And this is the meaning of
as it says in the Midrash (Koheles Rabbah 1:16):
as it says, 'And my heart saw'" (Koheles 1:16).
is the aspect of the middah
מִפַּחַד ה׳ וַהֲדַר גְּאוֹנוֹ (יְשַׁעְיָה ב, י).
"from fear of Hashem and from the splendor of His majesty" (Yeshayah 2:10).
And it is called by the name "flames"
according to the allusion mentioned above
"once they were arranged to be seen, etc.";
the aspect of "the Fear of Yitzchak"
one comes to a greater revelation,
HaKadosh Baruch Hu with their own eyes."
to gather them from the four corners of the earth,
so that no outcast be banished from Him,
of the sound of a great shofar,
"And it shall be on that day
that a great shofar shall be sounded,
and those lost in the land of Ashur shall come,
and those cast away in the land of Mitzrayim" (Yeshayah 27:13).
these are the ones assimilated among the nations
who do not know at all
and they are the Ten Tribes.
so that they not remain behind,
for whoever is of the seed of Yaakov
will not be lost, chas v'shalom.
"And those cast away in the land of Mitzrayim" —
these are the ones sunk in desires,
like a fetus in its mother's womb;
and the kelipah of Mitzrayim is in desires,
as it is called "the nakedness of Mitzrayim";
but they know that they are of Yisrael;
and for them too the great shofar will help.
And all the nations are called
עַל שֵׁם אַשּׁוּר וְעַל שֵׁם מִצְרַיִם,
by the name of Ashur and by the name of Mitzrayim,
And as we have spoken of this,
that it is alluded to in the blessing of Yaakov:
"And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth" —
when they will be in utter lowliness, like dust —
וּפָרַצְתָּ יָמָּה וָקֵדְמָה וְגוֹ׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, יד),
"and you shall spread out to the west and to the east, etc." (Bereishis 28:14);
that is, an inheritance without boundaries.
who raised up the yoke of teshuvah."
is the utmost darkness and concealment,
That is, even if one has corrupted his deeds,
until he has drawn upon his soul
גַּם חֹשֶׁךְ לֹא יַחְשִׁיךְ מִמְּךָ וְגוֹ׳ (תְּהִלִּים קלט, יב);
"even darkness does not darken from You, etc." (Tehillim 139:12);
for it is in the power of a Jewish soul
so that all be turned to good.
